chapter_seo_title: Desolate Era Ch. 445: The Eve of War – Ji Ning Prepares to Attack the Shaoyin Clan
chapter_meta_description: Ji Ning refuses his cousin's suicidal plea for revenge and prepares to assault the Shaoyin clan's lair. A million cultivators stand in his way.
og_title: Desolate Era 445: The Eve of War
og_description: Ji Ning's quiet night before the storm. A million enemies await.
twitter_title: Desolate Era Ch. 445 - The Eve of War
twitter_description: The calm before the storm. Ji Ning says goodbye to peace and prepares to invade an ancient clan's lair.

lore_anchors.definition: A flame of pure cosmic judgment that burns a cultivator from the soul outward, triggered by the sin of mass slaughter. It ignores physical defenses and can kill even Immortals, serving as the universe's ultimate deterrent against genocide.

The supreme defensive divine ability, granting its user an indestructible body that can ignore attacks from powerful foes. At the fifth stage, it allows Ji Ning to contemplate a frontal assault on a lair of millions.

A Xianxia trope representing the numerical might of a top-tier ancient clan. While most are low-level, their sheer numbers and layered formations make a lair nearly impossible for a normal Immortal to assault.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Ji Ning refuse to let Yuchi Xiyue come?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because slaughtering mortals would cover her in such heavy karmic sin that the resulting hellfire would instantly incinerate her Primal Daoist soul, no matter how justified her vengeance is.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the significance of the 'million cultivators' in the Shaoyin clan's lair?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It highlights the impossible odds. While 99% are just Zifu Disciples, there are so many, backed by infinite formations, that a normal Celestial Immortal would die from attrition. Only Ji Ning's invincible body allows him to attempt this.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Mu Northson look like a 'shell of his former self'?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He has been broken by the trauma of his lover's death and his own helplessness. His only solace is the ritualized act of carving statues, and his breakdown upon seeing Ji Ning is raw and animalistic.
